text:
Raj (People Ops): Hey team, follow-up from today's all-hands HR segment. Using this thread for rapid Q&A on reviews, promotions, comp timing, and benefits clarifications for the next 90 minutes. Policy links: https://intranet.redwood/people/promo-policy and benefits summary: https://intranet.redwood/benefits2026

Zoe (Eng): Quick one: if someone moves to part-time (60%) mid-cycle, how does that affect their review and compensation for this cycle?

Elaine (People Ops): Short answer: performance review still happens on schedule. Compensation will be pro-rated from the effective date of FTE change. If promo approved retroactive to pre-change, comp is adjusted to reflect FTE for the payout. DM us for edge cases.

Omar (Manager): For calibration, can we escalate a case if a peer group reasonably disagrees with the initial band recommendation? What's the appeals path?

Raj (People Ops): Yes. There's a 48-hr appeals window after calibrations close. Appeals require manager write-up + one peer manager endorsement. Appeals go to the org-level panel (People Ops + two senior engineering managers). We'll add the appeals form link to the rubric doc.

benefits-bot: Reminder: Open enrollment webinar tomorrow 11:00am PT -> https://calendar.redwood/open-enroll?w=webinar :calendar:

Carla (Finance): Note on bonuses: any performance bonus adjustments from this review cycle will be paid on the July 1 payroll run. If comp letters change between now and payroll, let People Ops know by 2026-06-20 to ensure correct payouts.

Diego (Recruiter): Hiring note: if a candidate has a verbal offer and the internal promotion for their hiring manager is pending, should we hold offers? We're seeing timing conflicts.

Elaine (People Ops): Don't hold offers for manager promos unless the promo materially changes approval authority for that role. In that case, loop in Recruiting and People Ops and we'll advise. Use this escalation tag: #promo-blocker.

Zoe (Eng): Parental leave follow-up: are we adjusting the phased return policy? Some folks requested longer phased return at 60% over 6 months.

Raj (People Ops): We piloted extended phased return for Q1 teams. Policy currently permits manager-approved phased returns up to 6 months at reduced FTE. These are evaluated case-by-case; submit the phased-return request form. For consistency, include a proposed ramp schedule and coverage plan.

Omar (Manager): One more: manager calibration meetingsare they recorded for on-call folks who can't attend?

Elaine (People Ops): Yes, recorded and minutes posted. But note: final calibration votes require the named managers to confirm in the form if they missed the live session. We'll send the recording and a short debrief doc.

Zoe (Eng): Thanks. Also, is there a standard comms template for notifying a team about an internal promotion before the official comp letter lands?

Raj (People Ops): We have two templates: one for level-only communications and one for level+comp. Use level-only when comp unknown. Snippet:

```
Hi team — quick update: [Name] has been approved for promotion to [New Level], effective [date]. Compensation details are being finalized and will be shared when available.
```

Use the comms kit in the playbook.

Carla (Finance): Clarification: equity refreshes tied to promos this cycle are limited due to pool constraints. If you believe a promo requires an equity grant to retain the person, mark as "equity-critical" in the submission form and tag Finance. We'll review prioritization daily.

Diego (Recruiter): Thx. Does internal transfer to a different role reset the review clock? Candidate moving teams next month.

Elaine (People Ops): Transfers do not reset the standard review cycle. If the transfer includes a level change, treat as a promotion submission. If the transfer is lateral, include a note in the review comments.

Zoe (Eng): Appreciate it. One tiny ask: can People Ops share anonymized examples of borderline promotions (what tipped them over)? That helps managers prepare evidence.

Raj (People Ops): Yes, posting two anonymized examples and a short checklist to the promo policy doc in ~15 mins.

Carla (Finance): Last note: 401k employer match cliff removed starting Q3. We'll send updated plan materials in the benefits packet.

Raj (People Ops): Great questions. I'll compile these into a short FAQ and post after the thread closes. If anyone needs a private consult, DM Elaine or me. Thanks! :handshake:
